mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5% during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) over the past month signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST rises over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90.0, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 90.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals monetary tightening combined with weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer confidence and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE falls > 0.2pp during high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
